title: Deductible applied to patient
plain: The payer did not pay this amount because it was applied to the patient's unmet annual deductible. The patient, not the plan, is responsible for this portion of the bill.
causes: The patient has not yet met the plan-year deductible
The claim was processed before the deductible was satisfied
The patient's deductible balance was recorded incorrectly by the payer
fix: Confirm the remaining deductible balance with the payer or through eligibility verification
Bill the patient for the deductible amount
Offer a payment plan or financial assistance if needed
If the deductible was already met, send proof and request reprocessing

title: Coinsurance applied to patient
plain: Under the plan's cost-sharing design, the patient owes a set percentage of the allowed amount for this service and the plan pays the rest — that patient percentage is what this adjustment shows. Whether it applies before or after the deductible depends on the plan. It is not a denial of the service itself.
causes: The plan's coinsurance percentage applies to this service
The service is covered but subject to cost sharing
The claim was priced at the allowed amount and split per the benefit design
fix: Verify the coinsurance percentage and allowed amount on the remittance
Bill the patient for their share
Check whether a secondary plan or supplemental policy covers the balance
If the percentage looks wrong, ask the payer to reprice the claim

title: Copay applied to patient
plain: This is the fixed dollar copay the patient owes for the visit or service under their plan. The payer withheld it from the payment because it is the patient's responsibility.
causes: A flat copay applies to this service type
The patient has not paid the copay at the time of service
A copay was applied in addition to other cost sharing
fix: Collect the copay from the patient (point of service is ideal)
Bill the patient if the copay was not collected
Verify the copay amount against the plan's benefit summary
Confirm no duplicate copay was taken for the same date of service

title: Modifier doesn't match procedure code
plain: The payer says the modifier submitted with this procedure code is not a valid or appropriate combination. The service may be legitimate, but the coding as billed does not line up.
causes: The modifier billed is not valid with, or not allowed on, this procedure code
The payer requires a different modifier for the same service
The wrong modifier was reported for the service actually performed
fix: Review the code-modifier pair against current CPT/AMA guidance and the payer's policy
Correct the modifier and submit a corrected claim
Attach the operative note or procedure documentation if the payer requires it
If the coding is already correct, appeal with supporting documentation

title: Place of service inconsistency
plain: The place of service or the type of bill on the claim does not match how the payer expects this procedure to be billed. The service itself is not in question — the setting information is.
causes: Wrong place of service code reported for where the service was furnished
Type of bill is not valid for the setting (for example, facility vs. non-facility)
Telehealth or off-site service billed without the payer's required setting code
fix: Confirm where the service actually took place and compare it to the place of service billed
Correct the place of service or type of bill and submit a corrected claim
Check the payer's current policy for telehealth and non-facility billing
If the original coding was right, appeal with documentation of the setting

title: Procedure code conflicts with patient age
plain: The payer says this procedure or revenue code is not consistent with the patient's age on file. Either the code is outside the covered age range or the age itself is wrong.
causes: The procedure is age-restricted and the patient falls outside the covered range
A pediatric or adult-only code was billed for the wrong age group
The patient's date of birth in the payer's system does not match the chart
fix: Verify the patient's date of birth on the claim against the chart and the payer's records
Check the payer's age limits for the procedure or revenue code
Correct the age or replace the code and resubmit
If the patient does meet criteria, appeal with clinical documentation

title: Procedure code conflicts with patient gender
plain: The payer flagged this procedure or revenue code as not matching the patient's gender on file. This is usually a data mismatch rather than a problem with the care that was given.
causes: The procedure is gender-specific and the gender on the claim does not match
The member's gender is recorded incorrectly in the payer's system
A code was selected that is restricted to a different gender
fix: Confirm the patient's gender in the chart and with the payer
Update the payer's member record if it is wrong
Correct the claim or the procedure code and resubmit
Appeal with clinical documentation if the service was appropriate

title: Provider specialty doesn't match procedure
plain: The payer says the billing or rendering provider's specialty or taxonomy does not support this procedure code. Typically the provider is not credentialed or enrolled for that service type.
causes: The taxonomy or specialty code on the claim does not match the service billed
The provider is not enrolled or credentialed with the payer for this service
The wrong NPI or taxonomy was reported on the claim
fix: Check the provider's taxonomy code on the claim against payer enrollment records
Correct the taxonomy, NPI, or rendering provider and resubmit
Contact credentialing to add the missing specialty or service category
Appeal with proof of credentials or training if the service is within scope

title: Diagnosis doesn't match patient age
plain: The diagnosis on the claim is not considered consistent with the patient's age, so the payer will not link it to the service. This often points to a date-of-birth or diagnosis code error.
causes: The diagnosis code is age-specific and the patient's age does not fit
The patient's date of birth on the claim is incorrect
The wrong diagnosis was linked to the procedure on the claim
fix: Verify the patient's date of birth on the claim against the chart
Review the diagnosis codes for age-specific validity
Correct the date of birth or diagnosis and submit a corrected claim
Appeal with chart notes if the diagnosis is accurate as coded

title: Diagnosis doesn't match patient gender
plain: The payer says the diagnosis code is not consistent with the patient's gender on file, so it will not support the service billed. This is usually a demographic or code-selection error.
causes: The diagnosis is gender-specific and does not match the gender on the claim
The member's gender is recorded incorrectly by the payer
An incorrect diagnosis code was linked to the procedure
fix: Confirm the patient's gender in the chart and with the payer
Update the payer's member record if the gender is wrong
Correct the diagnosis or demographic data and resubmit the claim
Appeal with clinical documentation if the coding is accurate

title: Procedure not proven effective
plain: The payer considers this procedure or treatment experimental, investigational, or not proven effective, so it is not covered under the plan. The 835 may include a healthcare policy segment pointing to the specific coverage rule.
causes: Procedure is considered experimental or investigational
Payer policy excludes the treatment as not proven effective
Clinical documentation does not establish effectiveness
fix: Review the payer policy and any 835 healthcare policy segment for the specific rule
Check whether the service meets coverage criteria and gather supporting clinical documentation
Correct and resubmit with documentation if coverage criteria are met
If not covered, appeal or follow plan rules for patient liability

title: Inappropriate or invalid place of service
plain: The payer will not pay because the service was rendered in a place of service that is not valid or appropriate for that procedure. This is often a claim coding issue or a setting restriction.
causes: Wrong place of service code on the claim
Service performed in a non-covered setting
Payer policy restricts the procedure to certain settings
fix: Verify the correct place of service code for where the service was performed
Correct the claim and resubmit
If the place of service was correct, appeal with documentation of the setting
Update front desk or scheduling workflows to use appropriate settings

title: Multiple or concurrent procedure bundling
plain: The payer applied multiple procedure or concurrent procedure rules, so payment was reduced or denied for overlapping or bundled services. Examples include multiple surgeries, same-day diagnostic imaging, and concurrent anesthesia.
causes: Multiple surgical procedures billed together
Diagnostic imaging performed on the same day
Concurrent anesthesia services
Procedures the payer considers bundled
fix: Review the multiple procedure rules and any 835 policy segment
Check whether modifiers or documentation support separate payment
Correct coding or modifiers and resubmit
Appeal with operative or procedure documentation if services were distinct

title: Outpatient services around inpatient stay
plain: Outpatient services are not covered when they fall within a specified period before or after an inpatient stay. The payer may require these services to be included with the inpatient claim instead.
causes: Outpatient service provided too close to an inpatient admission or discharge
Payer's global billing period for the inpatient stay
Service should have been included in the inpatient claim
fix: Check the dates of the inpatient and outpatient services
Determine whether the outpatient service should be combined with the inpatient claim
Correct and resubmit the claim or appeal with medical records
Verify the payer's billing and timely filing rules

title: No second surgical opinion
plain: The claim was adjusted because a required second surgical opinion was not obtained before the surgery. The payer may require this as a condition of coverage.
causes: Second opinion not obtained before surgery
Documentation of the second opinion not submitted
Payer requires a second opinion for this procedure
fix: Obtain and document the second surgical opinion if still possible
Submit the second opinion with a corrected claim or appeal
If it cannot be obtained, appeal with an explanation
Update pre-operative checklists to include second opinion requirements

title: Patient blood deductible amount
plain: This is the deductible amount the patient owes for blood or blood products under the plan. The payer is applying a specific blood deductible benefit.
causes: Patient has not met the blood deductible
Blood products were furnished during the stay or procedure
Plan applies a separate blood deductible
fix: Verify the patient's blood deductible benefit
Bill the patient for the blood deductible amount
Apply payments to the deductible
Explain to the patient that this is a plan benefit requirement

title: Day outlier amount
plain: This is a day outlier adjustment: the inpatient stay ran longer than the payer's day outlier threshold, so payment was adjusted (usually increased) to account for the extra days. It is a payment calculation, not a denial of care.
causes: Length of stay exceeds the day outlier threshold
Payer's outlier payment methodology
Additional days are eligible for an outlier adjustment
fix: Review the outlier calculation and the 835 details
Verify the length of stay and patient status
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Cost outlier adjustment
plain: This is a cost outlier adjustment: the case cost far more than usual, so the payer adjusted payment (typically adding an amount) to compensate for costs above the plan's cost outlier threshold. It is a payment calculation for high-cost cases, not a denial.
causes: Costs exceed the cost outlier threshold
Payer's cost outlier payment policy
High-cost case reviewed for additional payment
fix: Review the cost outlier calculation
Verify charges and any supporting cost data
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Indirect medical education adjustment
plain: This is a payment adjustment for indirect medical education costs associated with teaching hospitals. It reflects the additional costs of operating a teaching facility.
causes: Teaching hospital indirect medical education adjustment
Payer's indirect medical education calculation
Claim processed under teaching hospital payment rules
fix: Verify the facility's teaching status and indirect medical education eligibility
Review the indirect medical education adjustment calculation
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice

title: Direct medical education adjustment
plain: This is a payment adjustment for direct medical education costs, such as resident training, at teaching facilities. It reflects allowable direct costs of medical education programs.
causes: Teaching hospital direct medical education adjustment
Payer's direct medical education calculation
Claim processed under teaching hospital payment rules
fix: Verify the facility's teaching status and direct medical education eligibility
Review the direct medical education adjustment calculation
If the adjustment is incorrect, request a review or appeal
Post the adjustment according to the remittance advice
